$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD). See aws/s3.json for the contract.

azure.entra.users.crud.title: Users (create, get, list, update, delete) over Microsoft Graph

azure.entra.groups.crud.title: Groups (create, get, list, delete, membership) over Microsoft Graph
limitations: Dynamic membership rules are stored but never evaluated — Vyomi only tracks membership added/removed explicitly.

azure.entra.applications.crud.title: App registrations, their auto-created enterprise application (service principal), and client secrets
limitations: Only the default Microsoft Graph User.Read delegated permission is seeded on every new registration; the API permissions / admin-consent workflow and OAuth2 token issuance are not simulated.

azure.entra.domains.title: Custom domain names (add, list, delete)
limitations: Added domains are never verified (isVerified stays false) — Vyomi has no DNS/TXT-record check to perform.

azure.entra.roles_and_administrators.title: Roles and administrators (built-in + custom directory roles, assignments)
limitations: Shares its evaluation engine with Azure RBAC (Microsoft.Authorization); directory roles are modelled as role definitions assignable at the tenant-root scope rather than through the real roleManagement/directory Graph surface.

azure.entra.directory_audit_log.title: Audit logs (directory mutations)
limitations: Only console/API-triggered directory mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); category/activity filtering and the date-range picker are not modelled.

azure.entra.organization_properties.title: Tenant properties (name, technical/privacy contacts, verified domains)

azure.entra.directory_settings.title: User settings (default user role permissions, guest access, LinkedIn connections)
limitations: 'Users can create security groups' = No really blocks POST /v1.0/groups for security groups (Microsoft 365 groups are unaffected); 'Users can register applications' = No really blocks POST /v1.0/applications — both return Graph's 403 Authorization_RequestDenied.

The real console only applies those two toggles to non-admin members; Vyomi has no signed-in-identity model to tell members from admins apart, so the toggle blocks every caller tenant-wide rather than just non-admins.

The remaining toggles (guest user access restrictions, restrict non-admin users from creating tenants, restrict access to the admin center, LinkedIn connections, show keep user signed in) are stored and returned exactly as set but not enforced — Vyomi has no tenant-creation flow, no separate admin-center surface, and no LinkedIn integration to gate.

azure.entra.sign_in_logs.title: Sign-in logs
limitations: Vyomi has no interactive sign-in flow to generate telemetry from; the page honestly shows no sign-ins rather than sample data.

azure.entra.security_defaults.title: Security defaults / Access management for Azure resources
limitations: 'Access management for Azure resources' = Yes really grants a tenant-root (scope "/") 'User Access Administrator' role assignment over the same Azure RBAC checkAccess engine every subscription's Access control (IAM) page uses — the real console's elevateAccess action. It is modelled for the single caller identity Vyomi has (no signed-in-admin model), not per-signed-in-user.

'Security defaults' (Manage security defaults) is a real Graph policy document (policies/identitySecurityDefaultsEnforcementPolicy) stored and returned exactly as set, but not enforced — Vyomi has no interactive sign-in flow to require MFA or block legacy authentication against.

azure.entra.devices.title: Devices (MDM/Intune-registered device inventory)
limitations: Device registration (MDM/WIP/BitLocker) is a distinct subsystem Vyomi does not model; no devices are ever listed.
